newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK, Japan sign investment protection agreement.
newsitem.headline: HK, Japan sign investment protection agreement.

text.p: Hong Kong and Japan on Thursday signed an internationally binding Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (IPPA), the Hong Kong government said in a statement.
The agreement was signed in Tokyo by Hong Kong Financial Secretary Donald Tsang and by Yukihiko Ikeda, Japan's Minister of Foreign Affairs, it said.
Under the terms of the IPPA, the two governments will provide for the equal treatment of investors, for compensation if investments are expropriated, and for free transfer of investments and returns.
It will also provide for the settlement of investment disputes in accordance with internationally accepted rules.

At present, Japan is the leading overseas investor in Hong Kong. As of 1995, investment from Japan amounted to HK$191.4 billion at original cost, representing 24.6 percent of total foreign investment in Hong Kong.
Hong Kong's accumulated investment in Japan was HK$202 million in 1995, accounting for 0.7 percent of total foreign investment in Japan.

The agreement was the 12th agreement that Hong Kong has signed in the area of investment promotion and protection. The territory has similar accords with the Netherlands, Australia, Denmark, Sweden, Switzerland, New Zealand, Italy, France, Germany, Belgium and Luxembourg, and Austria.
